Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

appeal verb and noun

an earnest call for help or support

also appeal to, appeal for help, make an appeal, call on, implore, plead

classical

Cic. Flacc. 4 (Lewis & Short): quem enim alium appellem? quem obtester? quem implōrem?
Cic. Quinct. 94 (Lewis & Short): cujus hominis fidēs implōranda est?

implōrō, implōrāre, implōrāvī, implōrātum

verb, first conjugation; the person, or the help asked for (auxilium, fidem), in the accusative

appeal to, call on for help; plead for

Festus explains it as asking with tears (Lewis & Short): an urgent appeal, to gods or to people. Fidem alicujus implōrāre, to appeal to someone’s good faith; auxilium implōrāre, to appeal for help.

Other words

  • appellō, appellāre, appellāvī, appellātum — call on, appeal to

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.188 (Lewis & Short): vōs etiam atque etiam implōrō et appellō; Traupman 272

    To go up to someone and speak to them, so also to call on them for help; its commoner senses are to address and to name (see address). In law, to appeal to a magistrate (see appeal, to a higher court).

  • obtestor, obtestārī, obtestātus sum — implore solemnly, call to witness

    verb, first conjugation, deponent; often with ut or nē + subjunctive · also used · classical

    To beg by all that is sacred, calling gods or men to witness; it stands beside implōrō in Cic. Flacc. 4 and Verr. 2.5.188 (Lewis & Short). For a plain “please”, see please.

Examples

  • quem enim alium appellem? quem obtester? quem implōrem?

    For to whom else should I appeal? Whom should I beseech? On whom should I call for help?Cic. Flacc. 4 (Lewis & Short)

  • mulierēs … quae ad proelium proficiscentēs mīlitēs passīs manibus flentēs implōrābant nē sē in servitūtem Rōmānīs trāderent

    the women, … who with outstretched hands and in tears implored the soldiers setting out for battle not to hand them over to the Romans as slavesCaes. B.G. 1.51.3

See also request, please, help!, address, appeal.
